citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let $A_D$ be the Dirichlet
Laplacian of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-dirichlet-diagonal-domain-identification]] with
$D(A_D)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\}$ and $A_Du=-D^2u$, and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$ with $\|V\|_\infty=\max_{[0,L]}|V|$. Let
$A:=A_D+M_V$ with domain $D(A):=D(A_D)$, where $(M_Vu)=Vu$ is multiplication
by $V$. Then:

(a) $M_V$ is bounded self-adjoint with $\|M_V\|=\|V\|_\infty$, $A$ is
self-adjoint on $D(A_D)$, and $Au=-D^2u+Vu$ for $u\in D(A_D)$;

(b) $A$ has compact resolvent: $(A-z)^{-1}$ is compact for every
$z\in\rho(A)$; consequently $A$ has a complete orthonormal family of
eigenvectors, all eigenspaces are finite dimensional, the eigenvalues
$E_1\le E_2\le\cdots$ (listed with multiplicity) satisfy $E_n\to\infty$ and
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$;

(c) with $\lambda_n=(n\pi/L)^2$ and $E_n(A_D)=\lambda_n$, the min-max
eigenvalues satisfy
$\bigl|E_n-\lambda_n\bigr|\le\|V\|_\infty\qquad(n\ge1).$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, with $V_{\min}:=\min_{[0,L]}V$ and
$V_{\max}:=\max_{[0,L]}V$. For $E\in\mathbb R$ let $u(\cdot,E)$ be the
solution of $-u''+Vu=Eu$, $u(0)=0$, $u'(0)=1$, and let $\theta(\cdot,E)$ be
its Prufer angle, as in [[thm-nrqm-intervals-prufer-energy-monotonicity]].
Call $E$ a **Dirichlet eigenvalue** when there is a nonzero
$w\in H^2(0,L)$ ([[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) with
$w^*(0)=w^*(L)=0$ satisfying $-w''+Vw=Ew$, $w^*$ the continuous
representative of [[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]].
Then:

(a) $E$ is a Dirichlet eigenvalue if and only if $\theta(L,E)=k\pi$ for some
integer $k\ge1$;

(b) for every $k\ge1$ the equation $\theta(L,E)=k\pi$ has exactly one
solution $E_k$; the sequence $(E_k)_{k\ge1}$ is strictly increasing,
$E_k\to\infty$, and it is exactly the sequence of Dirichlet eigenvalues, each
with one-dimensional eigenspace:
$\ker(-\tfrac{d^2}{dx^2}+V-E_k)=\mathbb Cu(\cdot,E_k)$;

(c) bounds: for every $k\ge1$,
$\Bigl(\frac{k\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2+V_{\min}\le E_k\le
\Bigl(\frac{k\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2+V_{\max};$

(d) nodal count: for every $E$, the number of zeros of $u(\cdot,E)$ in
$(0,L]$ equals $\lfloor\theta(L,E)/\pi\rfloor$; consequently the $k$-th
eigenfunction $u(\cdot,E_k)$ has exactly $k-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$, and the same
holds for every nonzero eigenfunction with eigenvalue $E_k$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let
$e_n(x)=\sqrt{\tfrac2L}\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad
\lambda_n:=\Bigl(\frac{n\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2\quad(n\ge1),$
let $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-sine-on-completeness]], and let $A_D$ be the diagonal
operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]
associated with $(e_n)$ and $(\lambda_n)$: $A_Dx=\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n
\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n$ with domain
$D(A_D)=\Bigl\{x\in L^2(0,L;\mathbb C):\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$
Let $B$ be the Dirichlet Laplacian
$Bu:=-D^2u,\qquad D(B)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\},$
with $H^2$ and the trace $u^*$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]
and [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]] clause (b). Then:

(a) $D(A_D)=D(B)$ and $A_D=B$; in particular $D(A_D)$ is a linear subspace of
$H^2(0,L)$ whose members have vanishing endpoint traces;

(b) $A_D$ is self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]),
positive, and its spectrum is $\sigma(A_D)=\{\lambda_n:n\ge1\}$; each
$\lambda_n$ is an eigenvalue with eigenvector $e_n$; the eigenvalues are
simple in the sense that $\ker(A_D-\lambda_n)$ contains no nonzero vector orthogonal
to $e_n$;

(c) for every $u\in D(A_D)$, $\langle A_Du,u\rangle=\|Du\|_{L^2(0,L)}^2$;
consequently $A_D\ge\lambda_1=(\pi/L)^2$ in the quadratic-form sense on its
domain.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix complex
scalars. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, bounded or
unbounded, and write $L^2(I;\mathbb C)$ for the complex Hilbert space of
Lebesgue (equivalence classes of) square-integrable functions with the inner
product $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_Iu\overline v$ linear in the first argument
([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).

**First-order space.** Define
$H^1(I):=\{u\in L^2(I;\mathbb C):\ \text{the weak derivative }Du\text{ of the class }u\text{ exists and }Du\in L^2(I;\mathbb C)\},$
where $Du$ is the weak derivative of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]: a class
$Du\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(I;\mathbb C)$ with
$\int_Iu\,\varphi'=(-1)\int_I(Du)\varphi\qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(I),$
an identity that is choice-free
([[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]]). Equip
$H^1(I)$ with the sesquilinear form
$\langle u,v\rangle_{H^1}:=\int_Iu\overline v+\int_I(Du)\overline{Dv},$
whose associated norm is $\|u\|_{H^1}=(\|u\|_{L^2}^2+\|Du\|_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}$;
the symbol $u'$ denotes the same weak derivative $Du$ throughout the page.

**Second-order space.** Define
$H^2(I):=\{u\in H^1(I):Du\in H^1(I)\},$
and for $u\in H^2(I)$ write $D^2u:=D(Du)\in L^2(I;\mathbb C)$; the norm is
$\|u\|_{H^2}=(\|u\|_{L^2}^2+\|Du\|_{L^2}^2+\|D^2u\|_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}$.
Thus $H^2(I)$ consists exactly of the classes in $L^2(I)$ whose first and
second weak derivatives exist and lie in $L^2(I)$, and $H^2(I)\subseteq
H^1(I)$.

**Endpoint-vanishing first-order space and the Dirichlet form.** For the
bounded interval $(0,L)$, $L>0$, define
$H^1_0(0,L):=\overline{C_c^\infty(0,L)}^{\,\|\cdot\|_{H^1}},$
the closure of the test functions in $H^1(0,L)$, and define the **Dirichlet
form** on it by $q_D[u]:=\|Du\|_{L^2(0,L)}^2=\int_0^L|Du|^2$.

**Elementary consequences, recorded for reuse.** Weak derivatives are unique
as locally integrable classes under Countable Choice, are additive and
$\mathbb C$-homogeneous, and classical derivatives of continuously
differentiable functions are weak derivatives. The cited published items
supply these facts, so $H^1(I)$ and $H^2(I)$ are well-defined linear
subspaces of $L^2(I;\mathbb C)$. No claim is made here that $H^1_0(0,L)$
equals the set of classes with vanishing endpoint values; that identification
is proved on this page from the trace estimates.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let
$e_n(x)=\sqrt{\tfrac2L}\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad
\lambda_n:=\Bigl(\frac{n\pi}{L}\Bigr)^2\quad(n\ge1),$
let $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the complete orthonormal family of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-sine-on-completeness]], and let $A_D$ be the diagonal
operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]
associated with $(e_n)$ and $(\lambda_n)$: $A_Dx=\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n
\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n$ with domain
$D(A_D)=\Bigl\{x\in L^2(0,L;\mathbb C):\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$
Let $B$ be the Dirichlet Laplacian
$Bu:=-D^2u,\qquad D(B)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u^*(0)=u^*(L)=0\},$
with $H^2$ and the trace $u^*$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]
and [[lem-nrqm-intervals-integration-by-parts]] clause (b). Then:

(a) $D(A_D)=D(B)$ and $A_D=B$; in particular $D(A_D)$ is a linear subspace of
$H^2(0,L)$ whose members have vanishing endpoint traces;

(b) $A_D$ is self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]),
positive, and its spectrum is $\sigma(A_D)=\{\lambda_n:n\ge1\}$; each
$\lambda_n$ is an eigenvalue with eigenvector $e_n$; the eigenvalues are
simple in the sense that $\ker(A_D-\lambda_n)$ contains no nonzero vector orthogonal
to $e_n$;

(c) for every $u\in D(A_D)$, $\langle A_Du,u\rangle=\|Du\|_{L^2(0,L)}^2$;
consequently $A_D\ge\lambda_1=(\pi/L)^2$ in the quadratic-form sense on its
domain.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$ and let
$L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$ be as in [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]].
Define, for $n\ge1$,
$e_n(x):=\sqrt{\frac2L}\,\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad x\in[0,L].$
Then $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ is an orthonormal family and a complete orthonormal
family (Hilbert basis) of $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]):
$\langle e_n,e_m\rangle=\delta_{nm},\qquad
\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_n:n\ge1\}=L^2(0,L;\mathbb C).$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
let $V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, and put
$D(A):=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u'^*(0)=\alpha u^*(0),\ u'^*(L)=\beta u^*(L)\},\qquad
Au:=-D^2u+Vu,$
with $H^2$, weak derivatives and traces as in
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]] and
[[lem-nrqm-intervals-weak-derivative-ac-representative]]. Then:

(a) $D(A)$ is dense in $L^2(0,L;\mathbb C)$, $A$ is well defined and
symmetric, and $A$ is self-adjoint;

(b) for every $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R$ there are unique $C^2$
solutions $u_a(\cdot,z)$ of $-u''+Vu=zu$ with
$u_a(0)=1$, $u_a'(0)=\alpha$, and $u_b(\cdot,z)$ with
$u_b(L)=1$, $u_b'(L)=\beta$; the Wronskian
$W(z):=u_a(x,z)u_b'(x,z)-u_a'(x,z)u_b(x,z)$
is independent of $x$ and $W(z)\ne0$;

(c) for $f\in L^2(0,L)$ the function
$u(x):=\int_0^LG_z(x,y)f(y)\,dy,\qquad
G_z(x,y):=-\frac{u_a(\min\{x,y\},z)\,u_b(\max\{x,y\},z)}{W(z)},$
lies in $H^2(0,L)$, satisfies the two Robin boundary conditions, and
$(A-z)u=f$. Consequently $(A-z)^{-1}f=u$, the resolvent is an integral
operator with continuous kernel $G_z$ on $[0,L]^2$, and $(A-z)^{-1}$ is a
compact operator for every $z$ in the resolvent set of $A$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $0<L<\infty$, $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$,
$V\in C([0,L];\mathbb R)$, and let $A$ be the Robin realisation of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-separated-robin-green-resolvent]]:
$D(A)=\{u\in H^2(0,L):u'^*(0)=\alpha u^*(0),\ u'^*(L)=\beta u^*(L)\},\qquad
Au=-D^2u+Vu .$
Then:

(a) $A$ has compact resolvent; there is a complete orthonormal family
$(\psi_n)_{n\ge1}$ of eigenvectors of $A$, every eigenspace of $A$ is
one-dimensional, and the spectrum of $A$ consists exactly of the eigenvalues
$\lambda_n$ of $A$, listed with multiplicity, which satisfy
$\lambda_n\to\infty$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$;

(b) in particular the eigenvalues can be listed strictly increasingly as
$\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\cdots$ (each simple), and if $A\psi=\lambda\psi$ with
$\psi\ne0$, then $\psi$ is a nonzero multiple of the solution $u_a(\cdot,\lambda)$
of $-u''+Vu=\lambda u$, $u(0)=1$, $u'(0)=\alpha$, and the eigenvalue
condition is $\beta=\tfrac{u_a'(L,\lambda)}{u_a(L,\lambda)}$ when
$u_a(L,\lambda)\ne0$, while $u_a(L,\lambda)=0$ occurs for no eigenvalue.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on an
infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-dimension]]), let $c\in\mathbb R$ lie in the
resolvent set of $A$, and assume that the resolvent
$R_c:=(A-c)^{-1}\in\mathcal B(H)$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Then:

(a) $H$ has a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of
eigenvectors of $A$; writing $\mu_n$ for the eigenvalue of $e_n$, one has
$|\mu_n|\to\infty$ (each eigenvalue repeated according to its finite
multiplicity), and every eigenspace of $A$ is finite dimensional;

(b) $\sigma(A)$ consists exactly of the eigenvalues $\mu_n$ of $A$ and has no
other points, and the essential spectrum is empty:
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]]); thus
every spectral point of $A$ is an isolated eigenvalue of finite
multiplicity;

(c) for every $z$ in the resolvent set of $A$ the resolvent $(A-z)^{-1}$ is
compact.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a
densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $c>0$ be
real. Write $cA$ for the operator with domain $D(cA):=D(A)$ and
$(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$. Then:

(a) $cA$ is self-adjoint.

(b) For every $z\in\mathbb C$ one has $z\in\rho(cA)$ if and only if
$z/c\in\rho(A)$, and then
$(cA-z)^{-1}=c^{-1}(A-z/c)^{-1}$; consequently
$\rho(cA)=c\,\rho(A)$ and $\sigma(cA)=c\,\sigma(A)$.

(c) If some, hence every, resolvent of $A$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]), then every resolvent of $cA$ is compact and
$A$ and $cA$ have the same complete orthonormal eigenfamily $(e_j)_{j\in J}$.
If $N:=\dim H<\infty$, take $J=\{1,\ldots,N\}$; if $H$ is infinite dimensional,
take $J=\mathbb N$, with $|\mu_j|\to\infty$ and each eigenvalue repeated
according to its finite multiplicity. In both cases $Ae_j=\mu_je_j$,
$(cA)e_j=c\mu_je_j$, and
$$\sigma(A)=\{\mu_j:j\in J\},\qquad\sigma(cA)=\{c\mu_j:j\in J\}$$
with no other spectral points. The finite-dimensional conclusion also holds
without a separate compactness assumption, since bounded operators on such
$H$ are compact.

(d) Eigenvectors correspond exactly: for $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in H$,
$x\ne0$, one has $x\in D(A)$ and $Ax=\lambda x$ if and only if
$x\in D(cA)$ and $(cA)x=(c\lambda)x$; and every eigenvalue of $cA$ has the same
eigenspace as the corresponding eigenvalue of $A$.

(e) If $A\ge\gamma$ in the quadratic-form sense, meaning that
$\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge\gamma\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, then
$cA\ge c\gamma$ in the same sense.

Only the scaling of the given operator is asserted; no domain, spectrum or
eigenvector is claimed for any other rescaling, and no physical
interpretation is attached.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

derivations.claim: [Dirichlet operator after scaling] The mathematical operator $A=A_{D}+M_{\tilde V}$ is self-adjoint with compact resolvent, complete orthonormal eigenfamily and min-max eigenvalues $E_{n}$, and $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)=\varnothing$ with $|E_{n}-\lambda_{n}|\le\|\tilde V\|_{\infty}$ by [F1]. Since $H_{D,V}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A$ with $c:=\hbar^{2}/2m>0$, [F6] gives that $H_{D,V}$ is self-adjoint, that its resolvents are compact, that the same complete orthonormal family consists of eigenvectors with eigenvalues $\mathcal E_{n}=cE_{n}$, and that $\sigma(H_{D,V})=c\,\sigma(A)=\{\mathcal E_{n}\}$ with no other spectral points; moreover the eigenvectors of $H_{D,V}$ are exactly those of $A$ by clause (d) of [F6]. The min-max bound gives $|\mathcal E_{n}-c\lambda_{n}|=c|E_{n}-\lambda_{n}|\le c\|\tilde V\|_{\infty}=\|V\|_{\infty}$, since $c\|\tilde V\|_{\infty}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)(2m/\hbar^{2})\|V\|_{\infty}=\|V\|_{\infty}$.

[Dirichlet eigenvalues are simple with the nodal counts] By [F2] the eigenvalue condition for $A$ is exactly the Dirichlet eigenvalue condition, so the eigenvalue set of $A$ is the strictly increasing sequence $(E_{k})$ of the nodal theorem, each eigenspace being one-dimensional and the eigenvector for $E_{k}$ having $k-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$. Therefore the min-max list $(E_{n})$ of step 1.1 is this strict sequence, the eigenspaces of $H_{D,V}$ are one-dimensional, and the eigenvector belonging to $\mathcal E_{n}=cE_{n}$ has exactly $n-1$ zeros in $(0,L)$.

[Robin model] By [F4] the mathematical operator $A_{\alpha\beta,\tilde V}$ is self-adjoint with compact resolvent, complete orthonormal eigenfamily, one-dimensional eigenspaces, strictly increasing eigenvalue list $\lambda_{n}$ with $\lambda_{n}\to\infty$ and no essential spectrum, and eigenvalue condition $\beta=u_{a}'(L,\lambda)/u_{a}(L,\lambda)$ with $u_{a}(L,\lambda)\ne0$. Scaling by $c=\hbar^{2}/2m$ via [F6] preserves all these properties with eigenvalues $\mathcal E_{n}=c\lambda_{n}$, strictly increasing with $\mathcal E_{n}\to\infty$, and the eigenvalue condition at $\lambda_{n}=2m\mathcal E_{n}/\hbar^{2}$ is unchanged, giving (b); the compact-resolvent transfer used here is the general statement of [F5].

[Free box] If $V=0$ then $\tilde V=0$ and $A=A_{D}$, so by [F3] the eigenvalues of $A$ are $\lambda_{n}=(n\pi/L)^{2}$ with eigenvectors $e_{n}$; after scaling by $c=\hbar^{2}/2m$ the eigenvalues of $H_{D,0}$ are $c\lambda_{n}=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}/(2mL^{2})$ with the same complete orthonormal eigenvectors $e_{n}$, and the nodal count $n-1$ is read explicitly from the zeros $x=kL/n$, $k=1,\dots,n-1$, of $e_{n}$ in $(0,L)$.

[Observable reading and scope] Both $H_{D,V}$ and $H_{\alpha\beta,V}$ are densely defined, self-adjoint and read their spectral coordinate in joules by [F7], so each is an assigned sharp observable in the sense of clause (a) of the definition of assigned observables; no further physical reading of the eigenvalues is made, and the exclusions of (c) are those stated in clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]]. This completes the proof of (a), (b) and (c).

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, $U>0$, $m,\hbar>0$ and put
$K:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar>0$. Let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $V(x)=-U$ for
$|x|\le a$ and $V(x)=0$ for $|x|>a$, and let
$H\psi:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\psi''+V\psi,\qquad D(H):=H^2(\mathbb R),$
with $H^2$ of [[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

(a) $H$ is self-adjoint on $H^2(\mathbb R)$;

(b) *root conditions.* $E\in\mathbb R$ with $-U<E<0$ is an eigenvalue of $H$
if and only if, writing $E=-\varepsilon$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m\varepsilon}/\hbar$
and $k:=\sqrt{2m(U-\varepsilon)}/\hbar$ (so that $k,\kappa>0$ and
$k^2+\kappa^2=K^2$), the pair $(k,\kappa)$ satisfies
$k\tan(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(even case)}\qquad\text{or}\qquad
-k\cot(ka)=\kappa\qquad\text{(odd case)} .$
Every such eigenvalue is simple, and its eigenfunction is, up to a nonzero
scalar, $x\mapsto\cos(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by $ce^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside
in the even case and $x\mapsto\sin(kx)$ on $(-a,a)$ continued by
$c\,\operatorname{sgn}(x)e^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside in the odd case;

(c) *range of energies.* There are no eigenvalues $E\le-U$ and no eigenvalues
$E\ge0$; hence all eigenvalues of $H$ lie in $(-U,0)$ and are given by (b);

(d) *bound count.* The number of negative eigenvalues of $H$ equals
$\Bigl\lceil\frac{2aK}{\pi}\Bigr\rceil,$
and more precisely the equations of (b) have exactly one solution $k$ in each
interval $\bigl(\frac{n\pi}{2a},\frac{(n+1)\pi}{2a}\bigr)$, $n\ge0$, whose
left endpoint satisfies $\frac{n\pi}{2a}<K$, and no solution in $(0,K)$
elsewhere; the solutions are alternatively of even type ($n$ even) and odd
type ($n$ odd).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$, whose completeness follows from [[thm-riesz-fischer-completeness-of-l-p]] and whose Hilbert-space structure is defined in [[def-hilbert-space]].

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=2\pi^2\hbar^2/m$, and let $H_0$ be the free one-dimensional operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) with $d=1$, this $c$ and $b=0$:
$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^{*}M_{c|\xi|^2}\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C):|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal F_2$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem and
$M_{c|\xi|^2}$ is multiplication by the function $\xi\mapsto c|\xi|^2$. Let
$D^2$ denote the second weak derivative, defined componentwise on the
locally integrable classes of $\mathbb R$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), and let
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ be the Sobolev space
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_0)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ as sets and
$$H_0f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,D^2f\qquad\text{for every }f\in D(H_0);$$
equivalently, $\mathcal F_2(H_0f)(\xi)=c|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f(\xi)$ and
$\mathcal F_2\bigl(-\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2f\bigr)(\xi)=c|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f(\xi)$
for almost every $\xi$, and the two $L^2$ classes agree.

(b) For every real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the operator
$H_0+M_V$ of clause (c) of the cited theorem, with domain $D(H_0)$, coincides
with the operator $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2f+Vf$ on the same domain; in
particular, for $E\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ the
eigenvalue equation $(H_0+M_V)\psi=E\psi$ is equivalent to the weak equation
$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ elementwise in $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$.

The statement identifies operators on the same domain; it asserts neither
smoothness of the classes in $W^{2,2}$ nor any physical interpretation.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,

and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7

**(b) The declared effective one-dimensional model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, adopt the **line model**. Its declared state space is
$$H_{\mathrm{lin}}:=L^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C\ \text{measurable}: \int_{\mathbb R}|f(x)|^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the complex Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes with the pairing
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}f\overline g\,dx$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Its declared
**position assignment** is the multiplication assignment $Q$, defined on the
classes with $xf\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, with the declared outcome law
$$\mu^{Q}_{\psi}(B):=\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R \text{ Borel})$$
for a unit class $\psi$. Indeed, the positive sigma-finite Lebesgue measure
space $\mathbb R$ and the finite measurable multiplier $x\mapsto x$ satisfy
[[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]] clauses (a)-(c)
under the choice assumptions of (a): $Q$ is self-adjoint on the displayed
domain, with spectral PVM $E_Q(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_B}$ and
$\|E_Q(B)\psi\|^2=\int_B|\psi|^2$. The probability reading of this
mathematical law is adopted under P2. Its declared **momentum assignment** is
$P:=-i\hbar D$ on the classes whose weak derivative $D\psi$ lies in

The pair asserts no derivation of $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, $Q$ or $P$ from the
three-dimensional model $H_{0}$ of P5: the reduction to one spatial dimension,
for instance by an idealized strong transverse confinement or by a declared
one-dimensional sector, is an assumption of the model. An assignment of a
concrete material system to the line model is an identification in the sense
of clause (iii) of P7 and carries the corresponding uncertainty.

**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be real,
bounded and measurable; write $\|V\|_{\infty}:=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|V(x)|$.
The **assigned energy operator** of the line model with potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}+M_{V},\qquad H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad c:=\frac{2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}}{m},$$
with $M_{V}$ the multiplication operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (a), on the common domain
$D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}})
=\{f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}\}$,
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a)-(c)). The declared energy unit is the joule. By
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain
$D(H_{V})$ is the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,D^{2}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$D^{2}$ the second weak derivative, so the model's time-independent equation
inside any open interval on which $V$ is (say) constant is the ordinary
differential equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$. The model
adopts $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its assigned energy observable in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a); its
self-adjointness is established by the line-model energy theorem of this page
and is not presupposed here. A declared potential is **compactly supported** when $V$
vanishes almost everywhere outside some bounded interval.

**(d) Bound states and stationary vocabulary.** A **stationary solution** of
the model with potential $V$ and energy $E\in\mathbb R$ is a nonzero class
$\psi\in D(H_{V})$ with $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$; the pair $(\psi,E)$ is an
**eigenpair** of the model. A **bound state** of the model is a stationary
solution with energy $E<0$ whose representative is normalized, $\|\psi\|=1$;
its eigenvalue $E$ is its **signed binding energy**, read in joules, and its
positive binding-energy magnitude is $-E$. The value $0$ is the reference
energy in this negative-eigenvalue definition of a bound state. For a general
bounded measurable $V$, this convention makes no assertion about the location
of any spectral threshold. The model reads the
energy outcome law of the pure preparation of a unit eigenstate $\psi$ with
eigenvalue $E$ through clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a)-(b):
for self-adjoint $H_V$ on the nonzero Hilbert space $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$,
its spectral projection at $E$ fixes the unit eigenvector, so the outcome
in $\{E\}$ has probability one and the law is the point mass $\delta_E$.
The position density of the preparation is $|\psi|^{2}$ by the
one-dimensional multiplication-PVM construction in clause (b) above. These
readings are declarations of the model under P2 and construct no sample,
detector or measured value.

**(e) Declared generalized stationary solutions.** Let
$-\infty=x_{0}<x_{1}<\dots<x_{n}=\infty$ be a finite partition of
$\mathbb R$, let $E\in\mathbb R$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and classically
$C^{1}$ on $\mathbb R$ with a continuous derivative, and twice continuously
differentiable on each open interval $(x_{j},x_{j+1})$ restricted to which
$V$ is continuous, satisfying
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''(x)+V(x)\psi(x)=E\psi(x)$ there. In addition,
require the stationary equation on the whole line in the weak sense:
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(x)\varphi''(x)\,dx+\int_{\mathbb R}V(x)\psi(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=E\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(x)\varphi(x)\,dx$$
for every smooth compactly supported real test function
$\varphi\in C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$; the equality is complex,
equivalently componentwise. All integrals are finite because $V$ and $\psi$
are bounded and the tests have compact support. This is exactly the assertion
$D^{2}\psi=(2m/\hbar^{2})(V-E)\psi$ with the weak derivative convention of
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]; it is required even
when $V$ is continuous on no open interval. For a piecewise constant potential
and a $C^{1}$ piecewise $C^{2}$ solution of the displayed classical equations,
integration by parts twice on the pieces gives this identity: the internal
boundary terms cancel by continuity of $\psi$ and $\psi'$, and the external
terms vanish by compact support of the test. Such a $\psi$ is
a **declared generalized stationary solution** of the model at energy $E$. It
need not be an element of $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$ (for example, a function
$x\mapsto A e^{ikx}$ with $A\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ and $k\in\mathbb R$
has constant density $|A|^{2}>0$, which is not integrable on $\mathbb R$). When it is
not in $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, it does not represent a preparation of the model
and clause (d) does not apply to it; its scattering reading uses only the
declared flux quantities computed from it, and every such use states the
idealization. Square-integrable solutions are not excluded: if the nonzero
class of $\psi$ belongs to $D(H_{V})$, the weak equation above is the
eigenvalue equation of clause (d), and its unit normalization has the
preparation and outcome-law readings of that clause. Merely declaring a
generalized stationary solution imposes no such normalization. For
dimensional bookkeeping, assign $\psi$ and its amplitudes
the one-dimensional position-wavefunction dimension $\ell^{-1/2}$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1 (the SI reference unit
is $\mathrm{m}^{-1/2}$); this convention does not normalize $\psi$ or make it
an element of $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$. The pair's scattering reading assigns to
$\psi$ the
**probability current** $j(x)=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{\psi(x)}\psi'(x)\bigr)$,
read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ by clause (d)5 of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and reads a ratio of currents at
infinity as a *transmitted or reflected fraction* of the incident current,
conditional on the declared solution and on the asymptotics displayed in each
statement; no such fraction is ascribed to a single particle and no count is
predicted.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the data of the pair: a declared
effective line model with a declared potential, energy operator, bound-state
vocabulary and generalized-solution vocabulary. In addition to P1, P2, P4, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics,
they adopt the effective line-model assignments of clauses (b)-(e); these
assignments are additional model assumptions and are not consequences of the
three-dimensional model. No numerical value of $m$, $V$ or $\hbar$ and no measured quantity is
asserted.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and

[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],

and spin label $s=0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $V:\mathbb
R\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, let $\|V\|_\infty=\sup|V|$,
and let $H_{V}$ be the assigned energy operator of clause (c) of the model,
with flow $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ and evolved preparations
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]. Then:

(a) $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model in the
sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]: $H_{V}$ is
densely defined and self-adjoint on
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$, and
$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}f+Vf$ for every $f\in D(H_{V})$.

(b) *Flow.* The family $t\mapsto U(t)$ is the model's strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group of the assigned energy observable; the
Schroedinger equation $i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{V}\psi(t)$ holds in the
norm-differentiable sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{V})$,
and for other vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not
asserted; density preparations evolve as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with
$\rho(t)$ a density operator for every $t$.

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure
preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and
only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{V}$; in that case, with eigenvalue
$E$, one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is
time-independent, and if $\|\psi\|=1$ the law assigns probability one to the
singleton $\{E\}$, so the energy mean exists and equals $E$, with second
moment $E^{2}$. Moreover every bounded assigned sharp observable compatible
with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in every preparation.

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit pure preparation $\psi$ the declared
position assignment of the model has outcome law
$\mu^{Q}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$ for every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$;
and if $\psi$ is a unit eigenvector with eigenvalue $E$, the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ coexist as readings of the same
preparation, of the action of the declared observables, without any joint
measurement claim.

(e) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
line model; it asserts no discrete spectrum or eigenbasis for a general
bounded measurable $V$, no completeness or scattering statement, no
identification of $H_{V}$ with any laboratory Hamiltonian beyond the tested

**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

derivations.claim: [Operator identity] By clause (c) of the line model the assigned energy operator of the well is $H_{\mathrm w}=H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}+M_{V}$ on $D(H_{\mathrm w})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$; by [F2] this domain is $H^{2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and $H_{\mathrm w}\psi=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+V\psi$ for every $\psi$ in it, and $M_V=M_{V_0}$ by [F1], so this is exactly the operator $H$ of [F1]. Therefore $H_{\mathrm w}=H$ as operators with the same domain, and [F1] gives that $H_{\mathrm w}$ is self-adjoint and bounded below by $-U$ in the quadratic-form sense.

[Bound state conditions] Since the operators coincide, the eigenvalue statements of [F1] clause (b) apply verbatim to $H_{\mathrm w}$: for $-U<E<0$ the eigenvalue condition is the even or odd root condition, every such eigenvalue is simple and has the displayed eigenfunction. By [F1] clause (c) there are no eigenvalues $E\le-U$ or $E\ge0$, so the eigenvalue set of $H_{\mathrm w}$ is contained in $(-U,0)$ and is given by the root conditions; by clause (d) of the model the bound states are exactly the unit eigenvectors with negative eigenvalue, with binding energy the eigenvalue, and by [F3] each is stationary with that energy. This is (b).

[Count] The count and branch description are those of [F1] clause (d) applied to $H_{\mathrm w}=H$: exactly $\lceil 2aK/\pi\rceil$ negative eigenvalues, one solution in each admissible half-period branch, alternating types, and no other solutions. Since $2aK/\pi>0$, the ceiling is at least one, giving at least one bound state; this is (c).

[Observable reading and scope] By [F3] the pair $(H_{\mathrm w},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable with the energy unit of [F4], and the position reading of a unit eigenvector is its density $|\psi|^{2}$; no laboratory identification is made, and the exclusions of (d) repeat clause (f) of the line model. This completes the proof of (a)-(d).
